title: As a developer, I can install a skill collection with one documented command — a package-manager one-liner, CLI, or in-agent marketplace command — and it is active in my next session
As a developer, I can choose install scope — project-local files committed with my repo, or user-global across all projects
As a developer, I can install only the specific skills I want from a collection instead of taking the whole bundle
As a developer, I can list what is installed and remove skills cleanly, without orphaned files or lingering instructions
As a developer, I can author a new skill from a documented template — a SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter — without reverse-engineering existing skills
As a developer, the collection ships a meta-skill or tool that guides my agent through writing, improving, and packaging new skills
As a developer, skills follow the open Agent Skills specification so the same skill folder is valid beyond this one vendor's tooling
As a developer, I can browse or search a catalog of available skills — a registry, leaderboard, or marketplace listing — before installing anything
As a developer, installed skills trigger automatically from task context, with descriptions engineered so the agent activates the right skill at the right moment
As an engineering-lead, I can distribute a standard skill set to my whole team — via a marketplace, a shared repo, or files committed to the project
As a developer, there is a documented update path — marketplace auto-updates or an explicit update command — so I get fixes without reinstalling from scratch
As a developer, releases ship with notes or a changelog so I can see what changed in the skills before I take an update
As an engineering-lead, I can control when skill changes reach my team — pinned versions or a lockfile rather than silent behind-the-back updates
As a developer, I can install the same collection into multiple different coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others — with per-harness instructions
As a developer, skills are plain markdown files and folders I can read, copy, and carry to another harness — not a proprietary binary format
As an engineering-lead, I can review exactly what instructions and scripts a skill will add — list contents before installing and read every file afterward
As an engineering-lead, the project documents its security posture — what skills can execute, the trust model for third-party skills, and any telemetry or data collection
As a developer, the collection maintains tests or evals for its skills so changes are verified against regressions rather than shipped on vibes
As a developer, the collection is actively maintained — recent releases, triaged issues, and accepted community contributions
As a developer, a quickstart takes me from nothing to a working installed skill in under five minutes
As a developer, every skill documents what it does and when it activates, so I can predict my agent's new behavior before it surprises me
As an AI-native user, my coding agent can install a skill by itself — a non-interactive, promptless install path an agent can run headlessly end to end
As an AI-native user, my agent can author and package a new skill end to end by following the project's own spec, template, or meta-skill
